subject: Post-call recap — Apertum Health inference constraints, topology options, and next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Pierce <devon.pierce@apertumhealth.com>, Alexis Chen <alexis.chen@apertumhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call recap — Apertum Health inference constraints, topology options, and next steps

Thanks for taking the time today — good conversation. Quick recap so we have the same working assumptions and a clear path for the technical deep-dive: 

High-level goals (as we took them down):
- Replace current on-prem microservice that runs document parsing + routing; target is 99.95% uptime and p95 latency <= 180ms for single-turn responses.
- Support burst traffic up to ~300 qps during peak business hours; sustained baseline ~60 qps.
- Data residency: patient PHI must stay in their VPC for the pilot; audit logs retained for 1 year.
- Model requirements: want a 13B-ish model for extraction accuracy today, but open to quantized 30B variants if latency can be met.

Technical constraints & key notes we captured:
- Strict p95 latency target (<=180ms) will likely require dedicated capacity near the workload (VPC/private deployment).
- Prefix/KV caching could reduce per-request compute by ~15–30% for your dialog-like traffic pattern.
- Throughput plan: continuous batching + autoscale to handle 300 qps bursts; need to confirm memory/sequence lengths for sizing.

Immediate next steps (agreed):
1) You share the latency profile CSV and a 24-hr QPS sample (Devon/Alexis) — we referenced aperture_latency_profile.csv today.
2) Marissa will draft a mutually scoped action plan (POC goals, timelines, success metrics) and share a one-page M.A.P.
3) Karthik and I will run a rough sizing exercise once we have the sample traffic + model choice, then propose two topology options (VPC private deployment vs Dedicated with regional peering).

Attachments: I included placeholder filenames we discussed — attach real samples when you can.

If anything above is off, flag it and we’ll adjust. Proposed timing: deep-dive next week (45–60m) to go through topology trade-offs and a preliminary capacity figure. Let me know your availability.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake | Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jordan — useful summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) The 300 qps burst is across our entire fleet of inference nodes (ingestion + extraction). For the initial pilot we expect ~120 qps for the extraction route that will hit Redwood. The CSV Devon will attach shows the per-route split.
2) Sequence lengths: average token length for extraction requests is 80 tokens, 95th percentile 210 tokens.
3) Model preference: we favor a 13B distilled model if it gets us within latency targets; fallback is a 30B quantized variant.

I've attached the latency_profile and a 24-hr QPS sample. We redacted PHI from the payloads but left timestamps and rate metrics intact.

We are available next Wed/Thu mornings (PDT) for the deep-dive. Please propose a slot and we’ll lock it in.

Best,

Appreciate the data, Alexis — that token distribution helps a lot. Initial technical notes from an ops/sizing perspective: 

- Latency target mapping: given avg=80 / p95=210 tokens and p95 <= 180ms, a single 13B on A100-class GPU in a shared-hosted config will likely miss p95 when sequence hits 210 unless we rely on heavy KV caching or very aggressive batching. For deterministic p95 we should evaluate Dedicated or VPC private nodes with lower contention.

- Throughput sizing (rough, ballpark): to hit baseline 60 qps and allow 5x headroom for bursts (300 qps), we should consider either:
  a) Dedicated pool of 6 x rtx-based instances (quantized 13B) with aggressive batching + prefix cache; or
  b) VPC deployment with two availability zones, 4 large instances each, and a small burst pool that routes to Redwood-hosted capacity as fallback.

- Autoscaling & warm state: Recommend pre-warming KV cache for common prefixes (daily morning surge) and a scale-up policy triggered at sustained 20% CPU/GPU queueing for 30s to avoid cold-starts that spike p95.

- Model variant recommendation: start POC on quantized 13B (int8) and run quality checks against your eval set. If accuracy drop is >1.5% absolute on extraction F1, pivot to 30B-quantized in Dedicated tier.

Next technical deliverables we’ll produce before the deep-dive:
- Two topology sketches (Dedicated-focused and VPC/private-focused) with cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Preliminary capacity table (instances, expected qps per instance, expected p95 under sample traffic).
- A short checklist for Apertum to share (sequence length distribution by endpoint, sample requests, security checklist for VPC peering).

Marissa — I’ll hand the cost sketch to you after we align on topology. Alexis/Devon — thanks for the files; I’ll do an initial run against a local quantized binary to validate the p95 estimates and share numbers by EOD tomorrow.

Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
